q: Ability to retain the original form when the applied force is removed is called ____.
e: Ability to retain the original form when the applied force is removed is called elasticity. The name used here is elasticity.

q: Not only springs but also other objects such as threads and rubber bands have ____ property.
e: Not only springs but also other objects such as threads and rubber bands have elastic property. Elastic is what this statement is using.

q: Elastic limit is a limit, beyond which if an elastic object is stretched, it will not return to its ____.
e: Elastic limit is a limit, beyond which if an elastic object is stretched, it will not return to its original form. Original form is what this statement is using.

q: Robert Hooke, the English scientist, noted that when an elastic body such as a spring is stretched by a weight (or) a force, the amount of elongation of the spring is proportional to the ____ that produces it so long as the elastic limit is not exceeded.
e: Robert Hooke, the English scientist, noted that when an elastic body such as a spring is stretched by a weight (or) a force, the amount of elongation of the spring is proportional to the applied force that produces it so long as the elastic limit is not exceeded. Applied force is what this statement is using.

q: The amount of elongation is also called ____.
e: The amount of elongation is also called extension. The name used here is extension.

q: As long as the elastic limit of a body is not exceeded, the strain produced is proportional to ____ causing it.
e: As long as the elastic limit of a body is not exceeded, the strain produced is proportional to stress causing it. Stress is what this statement is using.

q: In symbols, $F \propto x$ (or) $F = kx$, where $F$ is the applied force (or) stress, $x$ is the elongation (or) strain and $k$ is a ____.
e: K depends on the units and on the permittivity of the medium. In vacuum K = 1/(4πε0) = 9 × 10⁹. In symbols, F ∝ x (or) F = kx, where F is the applied force (or) stress, x is the elongation (or) strain and k is a constant.

q: For a spring, $k$ is also called ____.
e: For a spring, k is also called spring constant. The name used here is spring constant.
The unit of k is Nm^-1. The unit written here is Nm^-1.

q: Hooke's law expresses the ____ behavior of materials.
e: Hooke's law expresses the elastic behavior of materials. Elastic is what this statement is using.

q: The work done is stored as the potential energy of the ____.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. The work done is stored as the potential energy of the spring.

q: The elastic potential energy stored by the stretched spring is also $\frac{1}{2}kx^2$. Thus, $W = \Delta PE = $ ____.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. The elastic potential energy stored by the stretched spring is also (1)/(2)kx². Thus, W = ΔPE = (1)/(2)kx².
